[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard provides **recommended guidance** for implementing protocol adapters in .NET 8 applications to enable communication between different protocols (REST, gRPC, SOAP, MQTT) and event-driven systems. Protocol adapters bridge legacy systems, external services, and IoT devices with the EaaS platform, enabling them to participate in event-driven architecture without requiring direct integration.
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope:**
- REST-to-Event adapters (HTTP webhooks → Kafka/RabbitMQ)
- gRPC-to-Event adapters (gRPC streaming → Kafka)
- SOAP-to-Event adapters (SOAP/XML → Kafka)
- MQTT-to-Event adapters (IoT device messages → Kafka/Redis Streams)
- Event-to-Protocol adapters (reverse direction: events → REST/gRPC/SOAP/MQTT)
- Protocol message mapping and transformation
- Adapter health monitoring and circuit breakers
- Correlation ID propagation across protocol boundaries

**Out of Scope:**
- Platform-level protocol gateways (see [STD-INFRA-INT-002](../../../infrastructure/integration/STD-INFRA-INT-002-protocol-translation-gateway.md))
- Direct protocol-to-protocol translation without event intermediation
- WebSocket adapters (future standard)
- File-based integration adapters (see STD-APP-INT-005)
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**RECOMMENDED** - Teams should follow this standard when implementing protocol adapters. Deviations are acceptable with justification but should be documented in Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

**Why This Standard Exists:**

1. **Legacy System Integration**: Many legacy systems use SOAP/XML and cannot be modernized immediately. Protocol adapters enable event-driven integration without requiring legacy system changes.

2. **External Partner Diversity**: External partners and vendors use diverse communication protocols (REST, gRPC, custom protocols). Adapters provide consistent integration patterns.

3. **IoT Device Integration**: IoT devices use MQTT for lightweight communication. MQTT-to-Event adapters enable device data to flow into event-driven analytics pipelines.

4. **Reduced Integration Complexity**: Centralizing protocol translation in adapters reduces complexity in domain services, which can focus on business logic rather than protocol handling.

5. **Event-Driven Architecture Benefits**: Adapters enable synchronous protocols (REST, SOAP) to participate in asynchronous event-driven workflows, improving scalability and resilience.

**Related Standards:**
- [STD-APP-INT-001: .NET 8 Integration Event Consumer](STD-APP-INT-001-dotnet-integration-consumer.md) - Consuming events from adapters
- [STD-APP-INT-002: .NET 8 Integration Event Publisher](STD-APP-INT-002-dotnet-integration-publisher.md) - Publishing events to adapters
- [STD-APP-INT-004: .NET 8 Event Transformation](STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md) - Data transformation patterns
- [STD-INFRA-INT-002: Protocol Translation Gateway](../../../infrastructure/integration/STD-INFRA-INT-002-protocol-translation-gateway.md) - Infrastructure-level gateways

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-001-adapter-architecture-pattern]

#### REQ-INT-003-001: Adapter Architecture Pattern

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Standardized adapter implementation ensures consistency, maintainability, and testability across different protocol integrations.

**Requirements:**
- Implement adapters as separate microservices or ASP.NET Core hosted services
- Use Adapter design pattern to isolate protocol-specific logic from business logic
- Implement bidirectional adapters (protocol → events AND events → protocol)
- Deploy adapters in Amazon EKS or AWS App Runner for scalability
- Configure horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) based on message throughput
- Implement graceful shutdown to complete in-flight message processing

**Validation:**
- Adapter deployed as separate service/container
- Protocol-specific logic isolated in adapter classes
- Both inbound and outbound directions implemented
- Deployment configuration includes autoscaling rules
- Graceful shutdown tested (30-second timeout minimum)

---
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-002-rest-to-event-adapter]

#### REQ-INT-003-002: REST-to-Event Adapter

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Many external systems use REST APIs and webhooks. REST-to-Event adapters enable these systems to publish events to EaaS platform.

**Requirements:**
- Use Refit >= 7.0.0 for type-safe REST client generation from OpenAPI specs
- Implement webhook receiver endpoint for REST callbacks (POST /webhooks/{source})
- Convert REST request/response payloads to events using AutoMapper >= 12.0.0
- Support multiple authentication mechanisms:
  - OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens
  - API Key authentication (header or query parameter)
  - Mutual TLS (mTLS) for high-security integrations
- Validate incoming webhook signatures (HMAC-SHA256)
- Implement rate limiting for webhook endpoints (default: 1000 requests/minute)
- Log REST request/response metadata for troubleshooting

**Validation:**
- Refit client generated from OpenAPI specification
- Webhook endpoint accepts POST requests with signature validation
- AutoMapper profiles defined for REST-to-event conversion
- At least one authentication mechanism configured
- Rate limiting configured and tested
- Request/response logging includes correlation IDs

---
page_texts.12:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-003-grpc-to-event-adapter]

#### REQ-INT-003-003: gRPC-to-Event Adapter

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: gRPC provides efficient binary serialization and streaming. gRPC-to-Event adapters enable microservices using gRPC to integrate with event-driven workflows.

**Requirements:**
- Use Grpc.Net.Client >= 2.60.0 for .NET 8 gRPC clients
- Implement unary RPC to event conversion (single request → single event)
- Implement server streaming to event stream conversion (single request → multiple events)
- Implement bidirectional streaming with event correlation
- Configure connection pooling with max 100 connections per endpoint
- Set keep-alive ping interval to 60 seconds to detect dead connections
- Handle gRPC status codes appropriately:
  - UNAVAILABLE → retry with exponential backoff
  - DEADLINE_EXCEEDED → log timeout and route to DLQ
  - UNAUTHENTICATED → refresh credentials and retry once
- Propagate gRPC metadata as event headers

**Validation:**
- gRPC client configured with connection pooling
- All three streaming types supported (unary, server, bidirectional)
- Keep-alive configured for connection health
- Error handling for gRPC status codes implemented
- Metadata propagation tested end-to-end

---
page_texts.13:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-004-soap-to-event-adapter]

#### REQ-INT-003-004: SOAP-to-Event Adapter

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Legacy systems predominantly use SOAP/XML. SOAP-to-Event adapters enable modernization without requiring legacy system changes.

**Requirements:**
- Use System.ServiceModel.Http >= 8.0.0 for WCF SOAP clients
- Generate SOAP client proxies from WSDL using `dotnet-svcutil`
- Convert SOAP XML payloads to event JSON/Avro using AutoMapper
- Handle WS-Security authentication:
  - Username/Password tokens
  - X.509 certificates
  - SAML tokens (if required by legacy system)
- Implement XML schema validation before conversion
- Handle SOAP faults gracefully:
  - Parse fault detail elements
  - Map to event error metadata
  - Route to DLQ with SOAP fault details
- Support both SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2
- Configure SOAP message size limits (default: 10 MB max)

**Validation:**
- WCF client proxy generated from WSDL
- SOAP-to-event mapping profiles defined
- WS-Security authentication configured
- SOAP fault handling tested with fault injection
- XML schema validation prevents malformed messages

---
page_texts.14:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-005-mqtt-to-event-adapter]

#### REQ-INT-003-005: MQTT-to-Event Adapter

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: IoT devices use MQTT for lightweight, efficient messaging. MQTT-to-Event adapters enable device data to flow into event-driven analytics and monitoring systems.

**Requirements:**
- Use MQTTnet >= 4.3.0 with ManagedClient for automatic reconnection
- Subscribe to MQTT topics using wildcards (e.g., `devices/+/telemetry/#`)
- Map MQTT topics to event types (e.g., `devices/123/telemetry/temperature` → `DeviceTemperatureEvent`)
- Handle MQTT QoS levels appropriately:
  - QoS 0 (At most once) → log and continue
  - QoS 1 (At least once) → acknowledge after event published to outbox
  - QoS 2 (Exactly once) → use two-phase commit with outbox
- Implement MQTT broker failover with multiple broker URLs
- Configure connection keep-alive to 60 seconds
- Set clean session to `false` to preserve subscriptions across reconnects
- Parse MQTT payload formats:
  - JSON (most common for IoT)
  - Protobuf (for efficient binary encoding)
  - Plain text with custom parsing
- Enrich events with MQTT metadata: topic, QoS, retain flag, timestamp

**Validation:**
- ManagedClient configured with automatic reconnection
- Topic wildcards subscribe to multiple device topics
- QoS levels handled correctly (test with QoS 0, 1, 2)
- Broker failover tested by stopping primary broker
- Multiple payload formats supported

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-006-event-to-protocol-adapter]

#### REQ-INT-003-006: Event-to-Protocol Adapter

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Event-to-Protocol adapters enable event-driven systems to invoke external APIs and legacy services, completing the bidirectional integration.

**Requirements:**
- Consume events from EaaS platform using [STD-APP-INT-001](STD-APP-INT-001-dotnet-integration-consumer.md) patterns
- Invoke external protocols based on event type:
  - REST: POST/PUT to external API endpoints
  - gRPC: Unary or streaming RPC calls
  - SOAP: InvokeAsync with SOAP request envelope
  - MQTT: Publish to external MQTT broker/topic
- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff (Polly >= 8.0.0):
  - Initial delay: 1 second
  - Max delay: 60 seconds
  - Max retry attempts: 3
- Handle protocol-specific errors:
  - REST 4xx → log error and route to DLQ (client error, no retry)
  - REST 5xx → retry with backoff (server error)
  - gRPC UNAVAILABLE → retry
  - SOAP fault → parse fault and route to DLQ
  - MQTT publish failure → retry with backoff
- Implement circuit breaker for each external endpoint:
  - Failure threshold: 5 failures in 30 seconds
  - Circuit open duration: 60 seconds
  - Half-open test: 1 request
- Log protocol invocation metadata: endpoint, latency, status code, correlation ID
- Propagate event correlation ID to protocol headers (REST), metadata (gRPC), or custom SOAP headers

**Validation:**
- Event consumer configured per STD-APP-INT-001
- All target protocols supported (REST, gRPC, SOAP, MQTT)
- Retry policy tested with transient failures
- Circuit breaker opens after threshold failures
- Correlation IDs propagated end-to-end

---
page_texts.16:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-007-protocol-health-monitoring]

#### REQ-INT-003-007: Protocol Health Monitoring

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Protocol adapters are critical integration points. Health monitoring detects connectivity issues and prevents cascading failures.

**Requirements:**
- Implement ASP.NET Core health check endpoints (`/health`, `/health/ready`, `/health/live`)
- Configure health checks for each protocol endpoint:
  - REST: HTTP GET to health endpoint (e.g., `/health`)
  - gRPC: gRPC health check service (grpc.health.v1.Health)
  - SOAP: Lightweight SOAP request (e.g., `GetVersion()`)
  - MQTT: MQTT PINGREQ/PINGRESP check
- Monitor protocol-specific metrics:
  - `adapter.protocol.requests` (Counter) - Total protocol requests
  - `adapter.protocol.failures` (Counter) - Failed protocol requests
  - `adapter.protocol.latency` (Histogram) - Protocol request duration
  - `adapter.protocol.circuit_breaker_state` (Gauge) - Circuit breaker state (0=Closed, 1=Open, 2=HalfOpen)
- Configure alerting for adapter failures:
  - P1: Health check failing for > 2 minutes
  - P1: Circuit breaker open for > 5 minutes
  - P2: Error rate > 5% for > 5 minutes
- Implement graceful degradation: if protocol endpoint unhealthy, queue events in outbox or DLQ

**Validation:**
- Health check endpoints return 200 OK when healthy, 503 when unhealthy
- Protocol-specific health checks configured
- Metrics exported to CloudWatch/Prometheus
- Alerts configured in monitoring system
- Graceful degradation tested by stopping external endpoint

---
page_texts.17:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#req-int-003-008-protocol-message-correlation]

#### REQ-INT-003-008: Protocol Message Correlation

**Status**: RECOMMENDED
**Rationale**: Tracking messages across protocol boundaries is essential for troubleshooting integration issues and ensuring end-to-end observability.

**Requirements:**
- Propagate correlation IDs across protocol boundaries:
  - REST: `X-Correlation-Id` header (inbound) → event `CorrelationId` → REST `X-Correlation-Id` header (outbound)
  - gRPC: `correlation-id` metadata → event `CorrelationId` → gRPC `correlation-id` metadata
  - SOAP: Custom SOAP header `<CorrelationId>` → event → SOAP header
  - MQTT: Include correlation ID in JSON payload `correlationId` field
- Convert protocol-specific headers/metadata to event metadata:
  - REST headers → event headers (e.g., `Content-Type`, `User-Agent`)
  - gRPC metadata → event metadata
  - SOAP headers → event headers
  - MQTT topic → event metadata `mqtt-topic`
- Implement distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry >= 1.7.0:
  - Create span for protocol request/receive: `adapter.protocol.receive` or `adapter.protocol.send`
  - Propagate W3C Trace Context (`traceparent`, `tracestate`)
  - Tag spans with protocol-specific attributes:
    - `protocol.type`: rest, grpc, soap, mqtt
    - `protocol.endpoint`: URL or broker address
    - `protocol.method`: HTTP method, gRPC method, SOAP action, MQTT topic
- Log protocol-specific identifiers:
  - REST: Request ID (if provided by external system)
  - gRPC: Call ID (from metadata)
  - SOAP: Message ID (from WS-Addressing)
  - MQTT: Message ID (from MQTT packet)
- Include correlation ID in all log statements using structured logging

**Validation:**
- Correlation IDs propagated from inbound protocol → event → outbound protocol
- W3C Trace Context headers present in all protocol invocations
- OpenTelemetry spans created for each protocol operation
- Structured logs include correlation ID and protocol identifiers
- End-to-end tracing verified in distributed tracing UI (e.g., Jaeger, X-Ray)

---
page_texts.19:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#adapter-deployment]

#### Adapter Deployment

- Deploy each adapter type as a separate microservice for isolation and independent scaling
- Use sidecar pattern for shared concerns (logging, metrics, tracing)
- Configure resource limits (CPU: 500m-2000m, Memory: 512Mi-2Gi) based on throughput
- Implement liveness probes (check adapter process health) and readiness probes (check protocol endpoint connectivity)
- Use Kubernetes Pod Disruption Budgets (PDB) to ensure minimum 1 replica during updates
page_texts.20:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#protocol-client-configuration]

#### Protocol Client Configuration

- Configure connection pooling for all protocols to reduce connection overhead
- Set appropriate timeouts:
  - REST: 30 seconds for standard requests, 5 minutes for long-running operations
  - gRPC: 30 seconds default, 5 minutes for streaming
  - SOAP: 60 seconds (legacy systems often slower)
  - MQTT: 60 seconds connect timeout, 10 seconds publish timeout
- Enable HTTP/2 for REST and gRPC clients (better performance with multiplexing)
- Configure TLS 1.2 or 1.3 for all production connections
page_texts.21:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#message-transformation]

#### Message Transformation

- Use AutoMapper for declarative mapping rather than manual mapping code
- Validate transformed messages against schemas before publishing events
- Handle missing/optional fields gracefully with default values
- Document transformation rules in mapping profile comments
- Version integration event DTOs independently from protocol DTOs
page_texts.22:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#error-handling]

#### Error Handling

- Implement different retry strategies per protocol and error type
- Use circuit breakers for external endpoints to prevent cascading failures
- Route unrecoverable errors to DLQ with detailed error context
- Alert on DLQ depth thresholds (e.g., > 100 messages)
- Implement compensating transactions for partial failures
page_texts.23:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#security]

#### Security

- Never log sensitive data from protocol messages (credentials, PII, PHI)
- Validate protocol message signatures (webhooks, MQTT messages)
- Use secure credential storage (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault)
- Rotate API keys and certificates regularly (90-day maximum)
- Implement IP whitelisting for webhook endpoints (if external system supports)
page_texts.24:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-003-dotnet-protocol-adapters.md#testing]

#### Testing

- Unit test protocol message parsing and transformation logic
- Integration test adapters with real protocol endpoints (use Testcontainers for MQTT brokers)
- Contract test protocol message formats against external system specifications
- Load test adapters at expected peak throughput (3x normal load minimum)
- Chaos test adapter resilience: kill external endpoints, inject latency, corrupt messages

### Compliance Checklist

- [ ] Adapter architecture implemented per REQ-INT-003-001
- [ ] Protocol clients configured (REST, gRPC, SOAP, MQTT as needed)
- [ ] Bidirectional adapters implemented (protocol → event AND event → protocol)
- [ ] Authentication configured per protocol requirements
- [ ] Health checks implemented for all protocol endpoints
- [ ] Correlation IDs propagated across protocol boundaries
- [ ] Retry logic with exponential backoff configured
- [ ] Circuit breakers implemented for external endpoints
- [ ] OpenTelemetry instrumentation added
- [ ] Unit tests cover protocol message transformations
- [ ] Integration tests validate end-to-end adapter flows

### Architecture Review

Submit to Architecture Review Board if:
- Implementing adapters for new protocols not covered by this standard
- Integrating with high-security legacy systems (government, financial)
- Deploying adapters at scale (> 10,000 messages/second)
- Implementing custom protocol translations beyond standard mappings
